![](figures/figureS_rise_factor_matrices/figureS_rise_factor_matrices.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label rise-factor-matrices >}}.
RISE factor matrices.** ({{< panel rise-factor-matrices factors genes >}}) RISE factor matrices representing component loadings of conditions and genes.
For visualization, genes outside the top 10% by weight in any component are omitted and each component is normalized to its largest absolute loading.

![](figures/figureS_cmp_stability/figureS_cmp_stability.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label cmp-stability >}}.
Collinearity and stability of RISE and CP components.** ({{< panel cmp-stability cp-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the condition, sender, receiver, and LR pair factors of any two CP components across ranks, as the median (line and points) and interquartile range (band) over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
({{< panel cmp-stability rise-fms >}}) RISE gene factor and ({{< panel cmp-stability cpd-fms >}}) CP LR pair factor FMS of each component across leave-one-patient-out jackknife replicates (n = 45), and, right of the dashed line, the aggregate FMS (mean over components) of each jackknife and re-initialization (seed only, n = 100) replicate.
Each replicate's components were matched to the reference's by Hungarian matching.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.

![](figures/figureS_nichenet/figureS_nichenet.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label nichenet >}}.
External validation of CCC-RISE LR weights.** ({{< panel nichenet ligand-scores >}}) NicheNet gene target scores of each ligand (n = 185) per CP component: the AUROC with which genes differentially expressed in the component's top receiver cells recover the ligand's predicted downstream targets.
Points are colored and sized by the ligand's weight in the component; opaque points mark the ligands of the component's top LR pairs.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
({{< panel nichenet weighted-percentiles >}}) Target-score percentile of each ligand among its component's ligands, each ligand counted in proportion to its ligand weight.
Boxes show the weighted quartiles, whiskers show the weighted 5th--95th percentiles, and diamonds show the weighted mean.
Null: the same percentiles on 1,000 copies of the NicheNet v2 prior with ligand--target links reassigned at random, pooled across components.

![](figures/figureS_alad_associations/figureS_alad_associations.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label alad-associations >}}.
Association of CP components, RISE components, and patient covariates with ALAD outcomes.** ({{< panel alad-associations cp-associations >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each CP component's condition loadings against each ALAD outcome.
\*: q < 0.05, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all outcomes and components.
({{< panel alad-associations death-weights >}}) CP component 4 condition loadings by ({{< panel alad-associations death-weights.1 >}}) six-month and ({{< panel alad-associations death-weights.2 >}}) one-year death.
Lines connect samples from the same patient.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
One-way ANOVA F and η^2^, with p Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all outcomes and components.
({{< panel alad-associations rise-associations >}}) As in ({{< panel alad-associations cp-associations >}}), for each RISE component's condition loadings.
({{< panel alad-associations sender-receiver-scatter >}}) Per-cell CP component 4 sender against receiver weight, with R^2^ across all cells.
({{< panel alad-associations covariates >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each patient covariate against each ALAD outcome, with binary covariates coded 0/1.
\*: p < 0.05, uncorrected.

![](figures/figureS_anova_stability/figureS_anova_stability.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label anova-stability >}}.
Stability of CP component--outcome associations.** ({{< panel anova-stability effect-size-distributions >}}) ANOVA η^2^ of each CP component's condition loadings against six-month outcome across leave-one-patient-out jackknife replicates (n = 45), each replicate's components matched to the reference's by Hungarian matching.
Diamonds mark the full-cohort η^2^, filled where q < 0.05.
({{< panel anova-stability significant-fraction >}}) Fraction of jackknife replicates in which each CP component's association with six-month outcome has q < 0.05.
q: Benjamini--Hochberg corrected p across the five components of each fit.

![](figures/figureS_ibd_rank_selection/figureS_ibd_rank_selection.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label ibd-rank-selection >}}.
IBD rank selection.** A) Schematic of the IBD cohort data\ [@doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7].
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection rise-rank-selection >}}) RISE R^2^X across ranks of the fit on all data and, in BiCV, of the fit on the training block (BiCV train) and its prediction of the held-out block (BiCV test); mean ± SD over 10 repeats per rank.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection bicv-test >}}) BiCV test R^2^X from ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection rise-rank-selection >}}) on its own magnified axis.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-r2x-starts >}}) CP fit R^2^X across ranks: the median (line) and range (band) over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
Circle: the elbow of the median curve located by Kneedle\ [@doi:10.1109/ICDCSW.2011.20].
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the LR pair factors of any two CP components across ranks, for each start (points), colored by whether the start reaches the solution most starts reach at its rank (blue) or another solution (grey).
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-minima >}}) Number of the 10 starts reaching each distinct solution across ranks (starts joined at FMS ≥ 0.95): the solution most starts reach (blue, bottom) and each other solution (grey), colored as in ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-collinearity >}}).
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection mode-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the condition, sender, and receiver factors of any two CP components across ranks, as the median (line and points) and interquartile range (band) over the starts.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection factors genes >}}) RISE factor matrices at the selected rank representing component loadings of conditions and genes.
J) RISE cell-type--eigen-state associations derived from RISE rank-60 projection matrices.

![](figures/figureS_ibd_associations/figureS_ibd_associations.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label ibd-associations >}}.
Association of CP components and covariates with IBD biopsy type.** A) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each CP component's condition loadings against each IBD biopsy categorization.
\*: q < 0.05, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all outcomes and components.
B--C) CP component B) 3 and C) 4 condition loadings by CD inflammation status.
Violins show [placeholder].
One-way ANOVA F and η^2^, with p Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all outcomes and components.
D) Fraction of each biopsy's cells in each coursely annotated cell type for healthy, CD uninflamed, and CD inflamed samples, on a square-root scale.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
q: Kruskal--Wallis test across the three groups, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across cell types.
E) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each patient covariate against each biopsy categorization, with binary covariates coded 0/1.
\*: p < 0.05, uncorrected.
